name: Awak
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only Kleinewillinghofer 2014/2020 comparative notes (Waja group); no grammar/phonology found

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Aspects of the phonology and grammar of the Yebu [=Awak] language in Nigeria. Draft circulated for comment, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge, 3 Jan 2020, ii+14 pp. (Wayback copy of rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/AU/Yebu phonology and grammar; the live domain is now squatted)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 Phonology = 3.1 Vowels (10-vowel ATR harmony, marginal length), 3.2 Consonants, 3.3 Tone (p.4): 'Yebu has three phonetic tone heights, but no minimal triplets, suggesting that underlyingly it is a two-tone system'; contrastive Low-High vs Mid-High rising tones; tonal morphology in plurals, verbs, possessives. The words stress/accent/prosody do not occur anywhere in the document.
